Machine Learning.summary: Machine-learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) for operational technology (OT) are commonly evaluated on benchmark datasets in which normal and attack data are collected in separate recordings. In such settings, high performance may reflect recording-associated differences as well as attack behavior. We introduce a recording-aware evaluation procedure that compares attack windows with background from the same recording, uses prior data for model fitting and calibration, tests temporal alignment against randomized event schedules, and reports event coverage together with alarm burden. On the ProvICS multimodal dataset, cyber modalities strongly distinguish the benign and attack recordings before the first labeled attack. Same-recording evaluation reverses the apparent modality ranking across all studied window sizes: the physical view becomes the strongest individual modality, while cyber-only fusion shows the largest difference between cross-recording and same-recording AUC, reaching 0.54. Operational analysis further shows that permissive event-overlap metrics can overstate detection when a small number of long alarm episodes cover multiple actions. An external analysis on HAI shows smaller and reference-dependent recording sensitivity. These findings show that cross-recording benchmark performance should be interpreted alongside same-recording, forward, temporal, and operational evaluations.
Machine Learning.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for presentation at the Industrial Control System Security Workshop (ICSS 2026), held in conjunction with the IEEE Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC 2026), Los Angeles, CA, USA, December 2026. Code and results are available at: https://github.com/ANTS-OntarioTechU/Recording-Aware-Evaluation-of-Multimodal-OT-Intrusion-Detection

Machine Learning.title: Data-Driven Resource Aggregation for Scalable Digital Twin and Simulation Model Generation
Machine Learning.summary: As industrial digitization accelerates, the use of digital twins has become widespread. However, modern manufacturing systems are highly dynamic and frequently reconfigured, making manual model development and updates increasingly difficult. Recent research on automated simulation model generation shows that historical data such as event logs can yield simulation models automatically. However, modeling every resource at full granularity leads to unnecessary complexity and computational cost. We propose a method for automatically selecting and aggregating resources to simplify simulation modeling. Our method uses ideas from inverse reinforcement learning to learn behavioral value representations of resources from production event logs. This process identifies and aggregates resources with similar functional contributions. Experiments on manufacturing systems, using throughput and system time as performance measures, demonstrate that value-based resource aggregation performs well when the goal is to substantially reduce complexity while preserving performance accuracy.

Machine Learning.title: Differential Refresh of Materialized Derived State: From a Single-Age Equivalence Limit to an Optimal Per-Partition Allocation, with a Real-System Validation on Materialized Views
Machine Learning.summary: Materialized views, cached aggregates, and trained models are all derived state: query results precomputed from base relations that begin to age the instant they are built, because the data they summarize keeps changing. A common way to keep such state fresh is to replace a fixed recompute cadence with an adaptive trigger -- a weighted staleness score that recomputes when accumulated base-data change crosses a threshold. We show this is the wrong lever and identify the right one. First, an equivalence limit: any refresh trigger that is a static, strictly monotone function of a single shared age of a globally-recomputed artifact is operationally equivalent to a calibrated periodic timer, so a global weighted staleness budget cannot schedule a recompute that a uniform timer could not. The escape is to enlarge the state: refresh partitions (the groups of a GROUP BY, per-tenant views, or data segments) differentially, each on its own schedule. We solve the resulting budget-allocation problem: the optimal per-partition recompute rate is proportional to the square root of partition risk sqrt(w_j*lambda_j), and the policy never costs more than the uniform timer, beating it by a closed-form Cauchy-Schwarz "price of uniformity" that grows with heterogeneity. We validate three ways -- analytic, discrete-event simulation, and a real relational engine (SQLite) maintaining materialized GROUP BY views with real SQL and wall-clock timing -- where the policy lowers realized weighted staleness by 14-15% at matched recompute count, winning on every run, while a naive per-partition exposure threshold does not reliably help. The rule for any periodically-recomputed derived state: a global staleness score is a timer in disguise; the leverage is differential refresh allocated by the square root of partition risk.

Machine Learning.title: On the Selectivity of Generative Models in Structure-Based Drug Design
Machine Learning.summary: Designing small-molecule drugs that selectively bind to a target protein while avoiding unintended interactions with other proteins is essential for reducing side effects that contribute substantially to clinical attrition. Although structure-based drug design (SBDD) has advanced rapidly with deep learning, most generative models still optimize binding to a single target and disregard selectivity due to limited training data and unknown off-target interactions. Motivated by this gap, we introduce SELECTBENCH, a comprehensive benchmark assessing the selectivity of generative SBDD models. SELECTBENCH provides three curated evaluation tasks reflecting different real-world drug discovery scenarios: literature-based case studies, safety screening panels used in pharmaceutical development, and large-scale structure-based evaluation sets. We further introduce a suite of metrics to quantify selectivity and conduct a systematic evaluation of nine representative SBDD models, including methods explicitly trained for selectivity and widely-used inference-time guidance techniques. Our results show that even selectivity-trained models achieve only modest off-target discrimination and inference-time guidance provides limited gains, underscoring the need for method improvement. SELECTBENCH provides both a characterization of where current generative SBDD stands on selectivity and an open, extensible platform to accelerate progress. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/lovetaro/selectbench.
Machine Learning.comment: Accepted as a Presentation at the Neural Information Processing Systems 2026

Machine Learning.title: Prefix-Tuning for Arbitrary Output Sequences on Pretrained Transformers
Machine Learning.summary: Prefix-tuning is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large language models (LLMs) that steers model outputs by prepending task-specific prefix representations to the input sequence. Despite its practical success, the theoretical understanding of the expressiveness of prefixes remains incomplete. In particular, the following question remains open: Given a pretrained autoregressive Transformer, for any input-output sequence pair $(\mathtt{x},\mathtt{y})$, does there always exist a prefix $\mathcal{S}$ such that prepending $\mathcal{S}$ to $\mathtt{x}$ induces the model to generate the target output $\mathtt{y}$? In this work, we prove that under the assumption that $\mathtt{y}$ is in the range of the pretrained Transformer, such a prefix $\mathcal{S}$ exists and can be explicitly computed by solving multiple linear systems. We further show that this assumption is necessary, in the sense that such a prefix may not exist when the assumption fails, thereby providing a complete answer to the above question. Our analysis is constructive and the obtained theoretical results hold under fairly general assumptions on model architecture. Extensive experiments on GPT-2 and Qwen3-4B demonstrate that our algorithm produces prefixes with strong control over model outputs.
Machine Learning.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Code: https://github.com/wzii/prefix_tuning. Online demo: https://wzii.github.io/prefix_tuning/

Machine Learning.title: Buffer-Parameterized Machine Learning Surrogate Models for Cross-Technology Signal Integrity Analysis and Optimization
Machine Learning.summary: Signal integrity (SI) analysis in printed circuit board (PCB) interconnects faces increasing complexity due to diverse integrated circuit (IC) buffer technologies, varying operating conditions, and manufacturing tolerances. Existing machine learning (ML) surrogate models for the prediction of SI metrics such as the inner eye contour, eye-height (EH), eye-width (EW), and transient waveform features often rely on fixed buffer parameters, limiting the adaptability across design and technology variations. This paper introduces a buffer-parameterized ML surrogate modeling methodology capable of handling cross-technology variations without retraining by treating IC buffer characteristics, e.g., clock frequency, supply voltage, rise/fall times, jitter, and internal resistors and capacitors, as model inputs in addition to the PCB parameters. To identify the optimal surrogate architecture for this high-dimensional space, tree-based methods (RFR/GBM), kernel methods (SVR/KRR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and neural networks are compared. The buffer-parameterized approach is validated using a complex interconnect with a total of 44 design parameters. In addition to demonstrating strong generalization, the results show that neural networks outperform other ML models on large datasets, while the anisotropic GPR excels in low-data regimes. Finally, the practical value of the ML surrogate models is demonstrated through a cross-technology design space exploration and optimization scenario, which indicates large computational speedups for eye mask compliance checking compared to simulation.
Machine Learning.comment: 12 pages, 16 figures, 7 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Machine Learning.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles
Machine Learning.summary: Variable roles describe recurring behaviors such as accumulation, traversal, and retaining the best candidate encountered. We use Sajaniemi's independently defined taxonomy to study which role distinctions can be recovered from large language models, how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) retain those distinctions, and whether associated directions support control of generation. We introduce static annotation rules for all eleven roles and a corpus of 126,926 natural-code files across five languages. Across five model-SAE systems, residual probes outperform individual SAE features and tested lexical baselines, with modest losses after neutral target renaming. Combining SAE features closes much of the single-feature gap, but probes on SAE reconstructions are less sensitive to role-changing edits reviewed by LLMs. High paired ranking accuracy coexists with frequent false positives at fixed thresholds. During generation, interventions often change role annotations at the cost of correctness; changes accompanied by passing tests show no clear aggregate advantage over random controls. The benchmark separates role-related recoverability, SAE fidelity, and correctness-preserving control through matched prediction, source edits, and generation interventions.

Machine Learning.title: Graph-Regularized Synthetic Control for Stable Counterfactual Estimation under Donor Redundancy
Machine Learning.summary: Synthetic control methods estimate counterfactual outcomes by weighting untreated donor units to match a treated unit before treatment. In recent applications, however, the donor pool can be large, highly correlated, and short in pre-treatment history, yielding many near-equivalent solutions with unstable and difficult-to-interpret donor weights. We propose Graph-Regularized Synthetic Control (Graph-SC), a convex estimator that augments the classical pre-treatment matching objective with a graph Laplacian penalty. The graph encodes similarity among donor trajectories, encouraging coherent weights over structurally related donors while preserving the transparency of synthetic controls. We provide theoretical results characterizing the bias-variance tradeoff induced by graph regularization and establish efficient convergence guarantees with an accelerated proximal gradient method. Across a controlled simulation under donor redundancy, the California Proposition 99 benchmark, and observational counterfactual analyses on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, Graph-SC improves weight stability, reduces sensitivity to redundant donor pools, and maintains competitive pre- and post-treatment accuracy relative to classical and regularized synthetic control baselines. Our results suggest that graph regularization is most valuable not as a universal accuracy booster, but as a principled mechanism for selecting stable and interpretable counterfactuals from near-equivalent synthetic controls with comparable pre-treatment fit.

Machine Learning.title: Looped GNNs Beyond Fixed Depth: Graph Size Generalization and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
Machine Learning.summary: Generalizing from small graphs to larger ones can require computation beyond the depth of a neural model used during training. We study target tasks that admit a common local iterative computation and whose effective dependency radius grows with graph size. The central idea is to learn a local update rule through GNN pretraining, then repeatedly apply the same learned processor beyond the training depth to extend information reach on larger graphs without retraining. Calling such parameter-shared architecture a \emph{looped GNN}, we categorize six schemes for looped GNNs to separate the effects of depth extension, fine-tuning, and freeze-and-steer adaptation. Our analysis establishes fixed-depth information limits and sufficient conditions under which accurate iterative reuse overcomes them. To improve beyond unadapted reuse, we introduce \emph{Loop-Freeze-Steer} (LFS), which freezes the pretrained processor and learns a small controller to steer its repeated application, using much fewer trainable parameters than full fine-tuning. Our finite-sample analysis gives sufficient conditions for adaptation to improve performance on larger graphs. Experiments on synthetic tasks and chip placement evaluate depth extension and adaptation, highlighting LFS's accuracy--trainable-parameter trade-off for size generalization.

Machine Learning.title: Interpretability of AI weather models via intermediate decoding
Machine Learning.summary: AI weather prediction models are often regarded as black boxes. Despite their impressive skill, there is little understanding of how the input data is processed during inference to produce the forecast. This limitation arises from the use of high-dimensional latent representations in which individual dimensions are no longer directly interpretable in physical terms. To gain insight into how forecasts are constructed, we propose the method of intermediate decoding for AI weather models and apply it to GraphCast, Aurora and ArchesWeather. In this approach, latent states from intermediate depths are decoded back into meteorological fields. To do this, we use the decoder that has been trained to output the forecast at the end of processing. Since latent states at different depths do not share a consistent basis, we train affine transformations that align intermediate latent states with the decoder's expected input space. Applying this framework to the three models yields the following results. First, the skill of forecasts at intermediate stages of processing improves gradually through the processor layers. Second, bypassing all processor blocks shows that the encoder-decoder pair is not an identity mapping returning the input, but instead plays a significant role in the forecast construction. Third, by examining increments of individual processor blocks across model depth, we show that all three models progressively refine the forecast from coarse to finer spatial scales. Finally, we assess the physical consistency of the intermediate decoding forecasts and find that large scales remain physically balanced throughout processing, while small scales become more balanced with each additional processor block.
Machine Learning.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Supplementary material in the ancillary files

Machine Learning.title: GLOW: General Linear Models Optimized with Ward's Method
Machine Learning.summary:
Neuroimaging seeks brain regions whose imaging features correlate with variables of interest (e.g., diagnosis, age), usually via the General Linear Model (GLM). Region-Based Analysis dilutes or splits any effect that does not fill exactly one atlas region. Voxel-Based Analysis, with Cluster Extent Thresholding and Threshold-Free Cluster Enhancement built on it, fits a GLM per voxel and groups adjacent significant voxels. But neighboring voxels can share a statistic without sharing a GLM, which a per-voxel statistic cannot detect.
  GLOW (General Linear Models Optimized with Ward's method) instead builds a hierarchy of nested regions by greedily minimizing GLM error (provably a special case of Ward's clustering). Maximum-statistic (Westfall-Young) permutation controls family-wise error over all regions. Significance spreads to an effect's nested fragments and the regions containing it; a final pruning step seeks whole, pure effect extents.
  We plant synthetic effects of known extent and varying strength in Human Connectome Project (HCP) diffusion images and in white noise. Pruning delivers wholeness: GLOW returns a spatially consistent effect as one region on 57% of HCP trials, the best baseline on 35%; baselines recover comparable volume, but in many pure pieces. The cost is positive predictive value (PPV): GLOW is more sensitive (by up to 0.29), but its regions overrun the effect, mostly because no hierarchy region isolates it, not because of pruning. On HCP, GLOW's mean Dice gains 0.059 over the best baseline at weaker effects and gives back 0.005 at stronger ones.
  On white noise, GLOW trails by up to 0.61 Dice: its hierarchy holds the effect, but its permutation test does not certify it. Runtime grows roughly linearly with voxel count, about 4.5 times the voxel-wise methods' on the full HCP volume. The PPV loss may trace to the assumption of spatially independent residuals.

Machine Learning.title: Location, Location, Generation: Where You Ask Matters for Generative Engine Optimization
Machine Learning.summary: Generative search engines answer local and commercial questions with a written answer and a few cited sources. A growing practice of generative engine optimization (GEO) monitors which sources and brands these answers show, typically from a single place. In this paper, we present a controlled audit of how the user's location changes the sources that generative engines cite. We ask 300 questions of ChatGPT with 19 declared locations, and of ChatGPT and Gemini from five network locations, each twice to measure run-to-run noise (31,200 answers). The engines take location from different channels. ChatGPT follows the location an application declares, down to the city: it writes the place into its own searches, and its search backend localizes results even when the queries name no place. It ignores the network. Gemini ignores the declared location and follows the country of the network, changing most of its sources even for questions that do not depend on place. The businesses the answers recommend change with the sources. Thus, visibility in generative search is specific to the user's location, and audits must control both channels.

Machine Learning.title: OrTeN: Neural Inverse Graphics for Joint Terrain and Line-scan Camera Trajectory Reconstruction
Machine Learning.summary: Digital terrain maps (DTMs) are used for landing site selection, terrain-relative navigation, and geological analysis in planetary exploration. Existing state-of-practice reconstruction techniques for creating DTMs from satellite imagery use multi-view stereo, requiring complex pipelines for dealing with camera error, changing illumination, and images with limited disparity. This work introduces Orbital Terrain Networks (OrTeN), a DTM construction method that uses neural inverse rendering to jointly optimize a textured height map and orbital camera corrections from line-scan satellite images. OrTeN operates directly on calibrated line-scan images with pixel values expressed as radiance factor (I/F) and corrects both broad trajectory pose inconsistencies and high-frequency pointing jitter jointly with surface reconstruction during training. Surface-projected patch normalized cross-correlation (NCC) enforces consistency between observations of the same terrain, refining an initial rough reconstruction. A semi-empirical reflectance model and shadow rendering are used to fit surface appearance from multi-date imagery with differing solar illumination. OrTeN requires only calibrated line-scan images and initial camera poses and does not use any structural priors including ranging/depth measurements or initial rough DTMs. OrTeN is evaluated on four planetary imagery datasets. Aligned terrain RMSEs are 2.35 m at Jezero Crater, 2.82 m at Gale Crater, 16.18 m at Olympus Mons, and 0.43 m at McGetchin Crater.

Machine Learning.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
Machine Learning.summary: Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) depends on unsafe multimodal data for post-training alignment or activation steering. However, such data is hard to collect, must be gathered anew for each modality, and its collection and distribution raise ethical and legal concerns. In this work, we relax this constraint and investigate whether textual refusal directions, extracted directly from the LLM backbone, generalize across modalities (i.e., image, video). Preliminary findings confirm this ability, though effectiveness is conditioned by layer selection, steering strength, and cross-modal alignment, with the latter causing safe multimodal inputs to be spuriously steered toward refusal. Building on this, we introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a lightweight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation centering, adaptively scales steering strength within a geometrically defined trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer, operating at the first generated token. Evaluated on five SOTA MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak, MARS achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility up to over-refusal. MARS reveals that safety-relevant structure is shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions are a powerful and underexplored foundation for multimodal alignment.

Machine Learning.title: ToolRosetta: Surface-Form Invariance of Tool-Call Guards
Machine Learning.summary: Step-level guards for tool-using agents are evaluated on tidy JSON tool calls, but deployed coding agents act through execute_bash and execute_code tools whose payloads are strings. We introduce ToolRosetta, which re-renders every candidate action in the AgentDojo and AgentHarm splits of TS-Bench as a Python call, as a shell command, and without the agent's rationale. The renderings are produced by code and verified by round-trip parsing, so the user request, the history, the label and the action's effect stay fixed while only the surface form changes. Across eleven guards with two placebo controls, frontier and strong open-weight guards are stable: no frontier error rate moves by more than 3.4 points. Four of five specialized agent guards are not: under the shell form their false-positive rates rise by 21 to 47 points on AgentDojo, and TS-Guard's by 38 points on its own home benchmark, blocking between a third and nine in ten benign actions; the fifth, StepGuard, does not move. A small open guard drifts five points more permissive. Removing the agent's rationale moves most guards whose input carries it, in guard-specific directions. A request-blind control on one guard shows that the rationale is where intent is read from. A parser that restores the canonical call in front of the guard removes the effect for these renderings, by construction. Benchmark accuracy on JSON calls does not predict a guard's operating point behind a code-acting agent.
Machine Learning.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild: Safety, Security, and Beyond (AIWILD). 4 pages plus appendices

Machine Learning.title: Alliance of Stochastic Routing and Reinforcement Fusion for Multi-Model Reasoning
Machine Learning.summary: This paper studies dynamic model routing under uncertainty in multimodal settings, where a system must select and potentially compose multiple models to answer a query. Standard reinforcement learning approaches for routing often suffer from premature convergence to suboptimal models due to noisy rewards and insufficient exploration. We propose a unified vision-language framework (VL-Scout) for efficient multimodal and multi-step reasoning with turn-based reinforcement fusion. First, VL-Scout combines Bayesian priors, policy gradient optimization, and sequential decision-making to enable structured exploration and adaptive inference. A context-dependent Dirichlet belief model allows for epistemic uncertainty over model quality and is updated online based on observed rewards and context-specific evidence, enabling Thompson-style exploration while serving as a prior for regularization. Second, a routing policy is trained via a KL-regularized REINFORCE objective by maximizing a reward-weighted evidence lower bound, where the policy acts as an amortized posterior, and the Dirichlet belief serves as a prior. Third, we introduce a fusion policy trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) or Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), which operates over intermediate model rationales and selects between two actions: CONTINUE or ANSWER, terminating with a generated output. We evaluate VL-Scout on four representative multi-modal benchmarks (MMMU, MMMU-Pro, OKVQA, and RealWorldQA), compared against 11 representative routing and policy optimization baselines. Our method provides consistent performance improvements while reducing premature policy collapse. These results highlight the importance of integrating uncertainty-aware priors with both amortized policy learning and sequential fusion for robust and efficient model selection in discrete action spaces

Machine Learning.title: Candidate-Label Saliency for Efficient Conformal Pruning of Text Classifiers
Machine Learning.summary: Recalibration can preserve conformal coverage after pruning while enlarging prediction sets and leaving more alternatives for downstream decisions. Directly searching for deletions that keep sets small is costly. We study whether a small candidate-gradient budget can approximate this search at lower cost. Candidate-Saliency Pruning (CSP) estimates the squared first-order change in two plausible labels' scores when each parameter is deleted. CSP averages these changes, combines the resulting importance with a base pruner, and selects the mixing weight under validation accuracy and coverage requirements. Independent split-conformal calibration supplies marginal coverage under exchangeability. We evaluate CSP on three classification tasks, two base pruners, and three sparsity levels against a squared true-label control that separates candidate choice from gradient squaring, under fixed recovery updates, equal total time, and restricted access to the training corpus. Before recovery, CSP reduces mean set size by 13.2\% to 19.2\% against the reference pruner and by 7.7\% to 13.2\% against the control in all six encoder cells at 50\% sparsity. The advantage over the control shrinks with recovery to practical equivalence in all six cells at 1,000 updates, and at equal total time the cheaper reference pruner is practically equivalent in 18 of 18 settings. When recovery is limited to the retained pruning pool, CSP keeps a meaningful advantage in all six cells. Its value therefore depends on the time and data available for recovery.

Machine Learning.title: What Remains Without Test Labels? Re-evaluating a Graph-Level Anomaly Detection Benchmark
Machine Learning.summary: Graph-level anomaly detectors are trained only on normal graphs, yet benchmarks may use test labels for model selection. We examine whether UB-GOLD results reused by later papers support label-free detection. We audit UB-GOLD and 14 GLAD code bases, re-run 21 detectors on UB-GOLD's folds under selection rules with and without test labels, and evaluate sensitivity to known structural changes. Test labels select checkpoints in UB-GOLD's shared training loop and checkpoints or hyperparameters in 8 of the 14 code bases. UB-GOLD also evaluates its kernel baselines against misaligned labels. Across nine datasets, selecting checkpoints by test AUROC adds an average of 5.12 AUROC points [3.97, 6.24] for the 12 UB-GOLD detectors relative to the final checkpoint and 4.13 [3.32, 4.79] relative to held-out normal graphs. In a post hoc permutation analysis with no truly better checkpoint, picking the best of noisy test evaluations still yields a gain more than half as large as the one observed against the final checkpoint. Configurations tuned on test labels score a further 1.53 points [0.64, 2.42] above repository defaults, a gap that mixes the value of test labels with that of tuning itself. With tuned hyperparameters and label-free checkpoint selection, the two strongest detectors retain their lead, while comparisons below them are less stable. Six of eight detectors evaluated out of sample miss size-preserving composition changes that graphlet counts detect. We recommend reporting results selected without test labels as the main comparisons and release per-run outputs that allow verification without retraining.
Machine Learning.comment: 68 pages (8 main pages), 7 figures, 54 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/Lu-Yujie/Label-Free-GLAD

Machine Learning.title: Client-Aware Security Adaptive Early Exit Vision Transformers for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
Machine Learning.summary: Federated learning (FL) trains a shared model across data-owning clients without centralizing raw data, but client data difficulty and compute budgets can differ. We study local early-exit Vision Transformer (ViT) inference, where an intermediate classifier may return a prediction before the final Transformer stage. The proposed method replaces one global acceptance threshold with a client-specific base threshold from label entropy and shallow-exit confidence, then adjusts each input using predictive entropy, confidence, top-two class margin, and exit depth. Aggregation uses only clients that updated a parameter. Security-aware routing reaches 88.70% CIFAR-10 accuracy with 32.0% depth saving and 73.7% ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy with 30\% saving. On matched six-client non-IID CIFAR-100, full-depth accuracy is 72.28% versus 68.20--71.80% for four heterogeneous-FL baselines; robustness-aware routing reaches 70.01% with 32.55% saving.

Machine Learning.title: Visual Causal-chain Bookmarking: Retrieval-Weighted Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Reward
Machine Learning.summary: RL agents trained on a single trajectory-level return face a credit-assignment problem: when a reward arrives many steps after the decision that caused it, every action gets the same signal regardless of causal responsibility. This paper studies Visual Causal-chain Bookmarking (VCBM), which concentrates credit on the decision points that determine an episode's return, via two instantiations. The first targets a fully observed, low-dimensional MDP (a delayed-reward watch-repair task), where VCBM statistically discovers which state components the agent causally controls and estimates per-decision-point action values directly, evaluated against ground truth and RUDDER, an LSTM-based baseline. VCBM converges to 95.07% correct decisions in a mean of 1,532.3 episodes across 20 seeds, versus RUDDER's slower, more variable convergence (mean 3,327.1 episodes; p<0.001); VCBM's discovered causal structure exactly matches ground truth in all seeds. The second targets a partially observed, language-based setting: an LLM agent trained with Leave-One-Out PPO (LOOP) in AppWorld, where causal discovery is intractable and a structural heuristic (state-mutating tool calls) substitutes for it, with credit distributed via retrieval over episodic memory and blended with LOOP's advantage. Over 200 iterations on identical Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct/LoRA/FSDP2 configurations, VCBM-blended LOOP improves task success over plain LOOP (0.354 vs. 0.458), reduces final-step max importance weight, and improves token efficiency, with a small KL exception favouring LOOP. The watch-repair result supports the claim that weighting causally relevant steps is more sample-efficient than an undifferentiated baseline or a learned return-redistribution network; the AppWorld result, limited to one seed per arm by a 2-GPU budget, is a compute-limited demonstration at a harder, natural-language scale, not a statistical confirmation.
Machine Learning.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. Master's dissertation research, University of Manchester

Machine Learning.title: When Does Evidence-Graph Structure Predict Answer Correctness? Label-Free Abstention for Structured Retrieval
Machine Learning.summary: Retrieval systems return scored answers, but a high score does not show that an answer should be trusted. The proposed training-free abstention method applies the boundary cut to the selected evidence in an evidence graph. The signal is the weighted cut between selected and unselected candidates and requires no correctness labels or confidence-model training. On MemoryAgentBench (MAB) FactConsolidation multi-hop, with unresolved queries ranked last for every selector, it raises area under the precision-coverage curve from 0.736 for the best score baseline to 0.785 (+0.049, 95% CI [+0.008, +0.092]); under the native evaluation, where score baselines keep their unresolved values, the gap is +0.108. A zero-cut subset contains 71 of 400 queries at 100% observed precision. In this pipeline, the subset corresponds to structural closure; controlled analyses attribute much of the remaining separation to resolution status, with little benefit from continuous edge weights. Across external benchmarks, usefulness varies with graph construction, edge semantics, and relation; typed structure alone does not ensure useful confidence. A supervised gradient-boosted selector achieves 0.814 versus the boundary cut's 0.785 when the retrieval stack matches. These findings provide empirical guidance for using available evidence graphs for lightweight, auditable post-retrieval abstention without additional model inference.
Machine Learning.comment: 34 pages, 5 figures, 37 tables. Under review at ACM Transactions on Information Systems

Machine Learning.title: Do Knowledge and Reasoning Oriented Benchmarks Induce Stable Representation Signatures in LLMs?
Machine Learning.summary: Internal signatures could support monitoring, adaptive computation, and mechanistic analysis, but benchmark prompts can be separable without any shared computational distinction. We test whether a prespecified knowledge/reasoning label defines a reusable internal signature in five contemporary 7B to 31B models. We treat the \textbf{task} as the unit of inference probes hold out complete tasks, labels are permuted across tasks, and the best layer and stream are reselected for every permutation. Raw probes recover an eight-versus-eight-subject MMLU partition in all five models (macro-F1 $0.78$--$0.81$), but prompt text predicts it nearly as well: under an identical probe configuration, the activation advantage is only $0.017$--$0.070$ macro-F1 and is not significant. At the prespecified $0.01$ level, lexical adjustment removes significance while the adjusted states still identify individual subjects, and the selected site changes across task panels and selection rules. Additionally, two released base-training trajectories show no common direction. These pooled layerwise measures recover the task label but identify no transferable knowledge/reasoning signature at the tested sensitivity, which cannot exclude moderate effects. The resulting protocol gives future internal monitors and intervention studies a sequence of tests to pass. Project page: \url{https://parsa-ra.github.io/lmbehave/}.
Machine Learning.comment: NeurIPS 2026 Interpretability as a Science Workshop

Multimedia.title: Learning to Reason About Implicit Multimodal Harm: From Diagnosis to Generalization
Multimedia.summary: A benign image paired with a benign caption can become harmful only in combination, making detection fundamentally a cross-modal reasoning problem. Existing multimodal harm benchmarks evaluate only classification accuracy, leaving unclear whether models identify the cross-modal mechanism that produces harm. We introduce MuPHI (Multimodal Pragmatic Harm Interpretation), a controlled diagnostic benchmark in which harm arises purely from image-text composition, with benign counterfactuals and annotated harm rationales. Using MuPHI, we systematically evaluate where compositional harm reasoning breaks in vision-language models (VLMs). MuPHI reveals that VLMs reliably ground each modality yet fail to bind the evidence into the harm mechanism and their predictions respond weakly to label-determining counterfactual interventions. Moreover, existing harm detection approaches trained on labels substantially improves in-domain (ID) detection but transfers poorly across harm distributions. We therefore propose Compositional Harm Interpretation Learning (CHIL), which rewards evidence identification in each modality, cross-modal binding and verdict consistency in the reasoning chain rather than just predicted label. CHIL improves 81% OOD transfer evaluations by an average of +2.5 macro-F1 and correct counterfactual flip rate by up to +3.8 and +5.4 % points, while also improving overall reasoning quality over label-only optimization. These results suggest that optimizing how a model reasons, not just what it concludes, offers a promising direction for multimodal safety systems that generalize beyond dataset-specific correlations.

Multimedia.title: TV-AudioRemover: Joint Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal with Multi-Task Hard-Mixture Curriculum
Multimedia.summary: Visual object removal can eliminate a target from video frames, yet its acoustic trace persists in the soundtrack, causing obvious audio-visual inconsistency. Existing video inpainting models operate solely on pixels, while audio editing models, especially for the sound removal task, are typically driven by text and therefore rely on limited single-modal control, which is less effective than multimodal guidance that provides stronger semantic grounding and temporal synchronization cues. In this paper, we present Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal (TV-AudioRemover), a target sound removal framework that leverages the visually edited video together with a natural-language instruction to suppress the sound associated with the removed visual object from the original audio mixture. To acquire high-quality training data, we devise a pipeline to construct a million-scale dataset of single-object audio-visual aligned samples, from which we synthesize mixture-target pairs customized for model training. To effectively leverage visual context and follow instruction intent, we augment the model architecture with task tokens, generalizable instruction modeling, and modality-specific global guidance. We further adopt multi-task training to strengthen task-role comprehension, and employ a hard-mixture curriculum that leverages semantically similar acoustic mixtures during fine-tuning to enhance fine-grained source discrimination. To support evaluation, we present AV-Remove-Bench, a comprehensive audio-visual object removal benchmark, along with dedicated objective metrics and an MLLM-based evaluation protocol. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both subjective and objective metrics. Project page: https://yjx-research.github.io/TV-AudioRemover/.

Multimedia.title: Semantic-Critical Regions for Video-to-Audio Generation
Multimedia.summary: In real-world videos, sound events are often associated with localized and fine-grained visual cues, such as object motion, object-part dynamics, contact events, and interactions between objects. Existing video-to-audio (V2A) methods employ implicit conditioning based on global visual representations or explicit control derived from temporal and spatial cues. However, subtle sound-producing and sound-indicative interactions remain insufficiently captured, leaving room for more precise visual conditioning of sound-event semantics and temporal dynamics. Motivated by this observation, we refer to regions containing such sound-relevant visual evidence as Semantic-Critical Regions (SCRs) and introduce SCR-V2A, a V2A generation framework that explicitly localizes and encodes SCRs as fine-grained visual guidance for audio generation. Specifically, we first identify SCRs through sound-related visual localization. We then transform the localized regions into a control representation through adapter-based dual visual encoding, which jointly captures global visual context and fine-grained sound-relevant evidence. The representation is used to condition a downstream audio generation model. Experiments on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks demonstrate that SCR-V2A achieves strong performance in distribution matching and audio quality while remaining competitive in cross-modal alignment and requiring few trainable parameters. These results highlight the value of prioritizing fine-grained, sound-relevant visual regions for V2A generation.
Multimedia.comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables, accepted by ACM Multimedia Asia 2026

Multimedia.title: Joint, Decoupled, or Agent: When Each Multimodal Alignment Paradigm Wins
Multimedia.summary: Jointly pretrained multimodal encoders are a common way to combine modalities, while alternatives integrate their information during downstream training or inference. When does each approach win? We compare three paradigms, instantiated with public checkpoints, across 16 paired datasets in five domains and multiple training-label budgets. JOINT trains a fusion head on frozen, jointly pretrained encoders. DECOUPLED trains a fusion head on frozen, independently pretrained encoders. AGENT gives a frozen LLM task instructions, labelled examples, available sample text, and supervised unimodal readouts. No paradigm dominates the complete 144 dataset-budget combinations: DECOUPLED wins 54, JOINT 44, and AGENT 46 by mean utility. ScienceQA, MELD, and MetMeme shift from AGENT to fusion as supervision increases. Between the fusion paradigms, JOINT leads on four of five QA datasets across all evaluated budgets, while higher unimodal 5-NN accuracy is associated with a relative shift toward DECOUPLED across eight classification datasets (Spearman $ρ=-0.67$). We test whether representation and task diagnostics predict these preferences on held-out datasets before fitting their candidate systems. A two-step cascade combines these diagnostics with task and budget metadata to select AGENT or fusion, then JOINT or DECOUPLED. Under leave-one-group-out evaluation, it selects the winner in 71.4% of cells versus 54.2% for metadata-only routing, with mean relative regret 0.028 versus 0.057. Using geometry, supervised representation diagnostics, and text-label matching together yields higher accuracy and lower regret than using any one of these sources with metadata. These results connect paradigm preferences to supervision budget, task format, and unimodal 5-NN accuracy. Target-task diagnostics thus support selecting among the three paradigms before candidate fitting.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275$\times$ less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains. Such tasks demand grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements obtained through heterogeneous tools, whose outputs must be made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps. We introduce OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness organized around a capability layer and persistent multimodal memory. The capability layer combines task-level tool interfaces with evidence rendering, providing consistent access to heterogeneous backends and converting their outputs into model-readable observations. Persistent multimodal memory retains the corresponding images, structured data, and web references as addressable artifacts throughout each query. A coding interface executes generated programs over stored data, enabling computations that combine results from multiple tools. Together, these mechanisms support an iterative process of acquiring, inspecting, and composing multimodal evidence. Evaluated on 22 benchmarks with eight open and proprietary backbones, OpenVLHarness improves average scores by 9.7-12.6 points over matched no-tool baselines, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra. With GPT-6 Luna at medium reasoning effort, OpenVLHarness outperforms the base model, Codex, and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort by 7.7-8.5 points while incurring at most 37% of their model-token cost.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this supervision with dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher equipped with an evidence-centered visual view. However, the resulting corrections may conflate visual evidence with non-visual shifts induced by linguistic priors, response style, or the privileged view itself. We formalize this phenomenon as privileged-correction contamination: a token-level correction is contaminated when its update direction cannot be consistently attributed to the privileged visual evidence. Directly distilling contaminated corrections may therefore reinforce erroneous token-level updates. To address this issue, we propose reinforcement learning with visually attributable on-policy self-distillation, an evidence-consistent paradigm that augments task-level RLVR supervision with privileged token-level corrections grounded in visual evidence. We instantiate this paradigm with Visual-Attribution Gating (VAG), which uses the verifier-derived advantage as the optimization anchor and validates each privileged correction against the contrast between evidence-present and evidence-degraded teacher views. By admitting only corrections directionally supported by this visual contrast, VAG preserves visually grounded guidance while suppressing inconsistent residuals. Experiments across six visual reasoning benchmarks show that VAG consistently outperforms GRPO and OPSD methods, establishing new state-of-the-art average performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion-based video matting has recently emerged as a leading approach, leveraging video diffusion priors from internet-scale pretraining to achieve strong zero-shot generalization from limited synthetic data. However, the heavy compute of these diffusion backbones limits inference to a short chunk of just 6 to 24 frames, so even ordinary videos span multiple chunks. Because each chunk is matted independently from coarse mask guidance, existing methods fail to maintain consistency across chunk boundaries, producing flickering edges and discontinuous transparency. We address this with a mask-guided diffusion-matting framework built on two ideas. The RGB and mask conditioning are represented as separate token streams that interact through full spatio-temporal self-attention, letting the model adaptively combine fine RGB texture with coarse mask layout rather than committing to a fixed channel-wise fusion. On top of this, we propose a novel pair of learnable embeddings, the preserve token and the refine token, that act as a per-frame conditioning interface and enable a sliding-window inference scheme in which already-generated mattes are propagated across chunk boundaries for local temporal consistency, complemented by a globally shared reference anchor at every chunk to prevent error accumulation in long sequences without any additional training. Across standard video matting benchmarks and in-the-wild long footage, our framework outperforms prior diffusion-based methods in both fine-detail accuracy and temporal consistency, and uniquely maintains consistency across chunk boundaries on long videos.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: InfiniDream: Open-Ended Photorealistic 3D Worlds Through Procedural Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Procedural generation plays a key role in synthetic data creation and game development, offering greater controllability, editability, and diversity than static mesh representations. However, VLM-based code generation often produces relatively simple 3D assets, while sophisticated photorealistic procedural systems require extensive manual development. Existing VLM-guided procedural methods remain largely constrained by predefined factories and APIs, limiting their ability to create novel asset types. We introduce InfiniDream, a VLM-driven framework for open-ended procedural 3D world generation. First, we propose Symbolically Constrained Asset Generation, which leverages existing procedural algorithms to create novel, photorealistic assets while preserving editability and seed-based diversity. Second, we develop an end-to-end text-to-world pipeline that combines semantic scene planning with Deterministic Frustum-Guided Grid Placement to construct large-scale 3D worlds with precise object placement, procedural population, and animation. Extensive evaluations on 100 object and 20 scene generation tasks demonstrate improvements across four perceptual metrics. Diversity analysis, ablation studies, and human preference evaluations further validate the effectiveness of our framework. Project page: https://yichuanh.github.io/infinidream-page/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Manga2Animate: An Agentic Framework for Faithful Manga Animation with Script and Storyboard Planning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Adapting existing manga into coherent animation that stays faithful to the source is a valuable yet challenging task. Existing methods either access the manga mainly through text, losing its characters and art style, or feed manga pages directly into video generation models, which misinterpret the manga's structure and produce incorrect storylines. In this paper, we propose Manga2Animate, a multi-agent framework that grounds every stage of generation in the source manga. We decompose the task into two intermediate representations, an animation script and a visual storyboard. Each representation is produced by a creator agent and reviewed against the source panels by a paired reviewer agent. We tailor representation-specific selection and dual-level feedback to progressively refine both before synthesizing the final animation. Extensive experiments and a user study demonstrate that Manga2Animate produces animations more faithful to the source manga and more consistent across shots than state-of-the-art approaches. Project page: https://annchenn.github.io/Manga2Animate/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GenOlympiad: Benchmarking Frontier Image Models at Their Capability Boundaries
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image models have made tremendous progress and can produce high-quality images. However, a question which would be asked in any other discipline is where the frontier models fall short. We introduce GenOlympiad, a benchmark which provides the most challenging text prompts from nine capability axes for stress-testing frontier text-to-image models. The assessed capabilities include generating large quantities, performing deep reasoning, ensuring hard physical consistency, following complex rules and so on. The prompts are designed such that prompt alignment is visually verifiable (e.g., counting) instead of relying on subjectiveness (e.g., style). Based on this, we develop an automated evaluation framework which decomposes the prompt into easy and hard questions, and for most hard questions, draws help lines to ground evidence for accurate grading. We evaluate 20+ strong text-to-image models, including Nano Banana Pro, GPT-Image-2.5, Seedream-5.0 and so on. We report that even the best-performing T2I model (Nano Banana Pro) only achieves a strict score of 23.9 out of 100 and that coding models such as GPT-6 Astra have higher prompt alignment scores (but not as visually pleasing). We also derive insights in model evolution, alignment with Elo scores, and effectiveness of our grounding-based evaluation protocol. Code is available at https://github.com/GenOlympiad/GenOlympiad and the project page is at https://genolympiad.github.io/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. Different VLMs are evaluated on 18 manipulation tasks under a fixed interaction budget. The analysis of experimental results motivates the Physical Barrel Hypothesis: different capabilities may constrain different parts of improvement. The five-axis metrics also distinguish systems with close public benchmark averages and show that high scores need not come with early or efficient gains. We study observational scaling from two perspectives: predicting the relative performance of VLM agents from their public capabilities, and forecasting later progress from early physical feedback. Together, these analyses ask how quickly and how far an agent can improve. Moreover, we conduct workspace interventions and then analyze what improvement leaves behind. Removing history reduces late-round success, frozen workspaces remain useful on unseen layouts, and three cross-task cases achieve success earlier. The results suggest that scene-specific adaptation and reusable experience can coexist.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: How Well Do Vision-Language Models Understand Movies?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can increasingly handle extended contexts and answer questions about long videos--but can they understand the narrative structure of movies as humans do? To investigate this question, we introduce MF$^2$ (Movie Facts and Fibs), a fully manually curated benchmark designed to evaluate whether models can identify, recall, and comprehend information central to the movie's storyline, using both the visual and textual modalities. MF$^2$ includes over 50 open-licensed movies, each paired with manually constructed sets of claim pairs: one true claim (fact) and one plausible but false (fib), totaling over 850 pairs. Our analysis across 20 open-source and 2 proprietary models reveals a substantial gap relative to human performance. While subtitles provide a strong signal for narrative understanding, other textual sources (e.g., synopses) are less informative. In contrast, when visual information is distributed across the entire movie and jointly embedded with subtitles, models struggle to identify and effectively use the relevant content. However, when the visual input is restricted to claim-relevant visual content, models improve significantly, indicating substantial room for improvement in processing large multimodal contexts and distinguishing relevant from irrelevant information. Overall, our findings highlight persistent challenges in multimodal narrative understanding for current VLMs. We release our data and code to support further research in this direction.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps. Recent forecasting methods extend this idea by extrapolating features to skipped steps instead of reusing them. However, existing forecasting methods extrapolate the features they predict uniformly, even though the spatial-frequency components of these features change most at different stages of denoising. They also overlook that denoising progresses nonuniformly, so equal step intervals can correspond to very different amounts of change. These mismatches amplify forecast errors as more steps are skipped, limiting the achievable acceleration. We propose SpecKCast, a training-free method that forecasts the model output in the frequency domain. SpecKCast applies a 2D discrete cosine transform (DCT) to the output and tracks each coefficient with a lightweight Kalman filter along a band-specific time coordinate derived from the noise schedule. The filter tracks each coefficient's value and rate of change, and the transformer is evaluated only when the filter's forecast uncertainty exceeds a threshold. Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B, and HunyuanVideo show that SpecKCast achieves a better trade-off between acceleration and fidelity than existing caching and forecasting methods, reaching up to 6x speedup with less than 0.05 GiB of additional memory.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Vision-language models see more about agriculture than they report, and test-time scaling remains bounded by parametric knowledge
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for agricultural diagnosis but fail unpredictably in zero-shot settings. We test whether this stems from poor visual features or an inability to verbalize what the model already perceives, using a benchmark spanning classification and detection drawn from 118 AgML classification and 54 detection datasets. Linear probing shows agricultural features are linearly separable in frozen VLM vision towers, with Gemma-4-31B's encoder reaching F1-macro of 0.60--0.78 across tasks and approaching the vision-only DINOv3 backbone, indicating the bottleneck lies downstream of perception. We then test whether test-time scaling, an iterative in-context skill-memory loop, can close this gap without updating weights. Gains are modest and inconsistent. Skill-memory improves classification accuracy by up to 3.1 points on three of four tasks while regressing on species, with gains concentrated on classes seen during optimization and unseen classes regressing. Detection F1 is effectively unchanged (0.412 to 0.421), though an oracle filtering condition reaches 0.432 F1, revealing real headroom unconstrained prompting fails to surface. These results indicate VLMs see more agricultural features than they report, but test-time scaling alone fails to surface that hidden parametric knowledge, motivating agentic approaches grounded in external, retrievable knowledge.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ICON decomposition: Multivariate concept auditing reveals shortcuts that neural networks rely on
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Deep neural networks often exploit spurious associations, a failure known as shortcut learning. Before deployment, models should therefore be audited for reliance on concepts such as acquisition artifacts and patient demographics. Current methods, including linear probes and concept activation vectors, measure concept reliance by asking whether each concept is decodable from a layer. We show that this framing is misleading: decodability reflects not only concept reliance but also correlations among concepts and the outcome in the auditing dataset. We reframe shortcut auditing as a decomposition of the variance of intermediary representations with Independent Canonical cONcepts (ICON). ICON quantifies the share of a layer's variance explained by each concept conditional on all other concepts and the outcome, and also reports the variance left unexplained. Because ICON explanations are comparable across layers, their trajectories distinguish concepts that drive predictions from those that are merely encoded in the representations. In simulated data with ground truth, ICON recovers concept importance more accurately than seven baselines. In skin-cancer and neuroimaging applications, it separates learned shortcuts from merely correlated concepts, which we confirm with independent validation checks.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 44 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables. Includes Extended Data (7 figures, 2 tables). Code: https://github.com/RoshanRane/ICON_decomposition

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Beyond basic tool use and coding skills, effectively incorporating visual references into agentic generation is equally essential for applying AI agents to real-world productivity tasks. We study this crucial capability through webpage development, a practical and readily evaluable setting in which existing benchmarks remain largely idealized: they typically focus on reconstructing visual targets or generating webpages from textual instructions alone, overlooking the more common workflow of developing from visual examples. Specifically, we introduce RefCraft, a benchmark comprising 300 realistic multimodal webpage-development tasks that combine natural-language instructions with screenshots from one to five reference webpages. Agents must selectively interpret and utilize these references while rendering, visually inspecting, and iteratively refining their outputs. We evaluate the resulting open-ended artifacts using independently verifiable keypoints and complementary programmatic and VLM judges. Across nine frontier (M)LLMs, the strongest system achieves an overall score of only 52.12 out of 100, revealing that visual-reference-conditioned agentic generation remains a substantial challenge for current models in practical webpage-development settings.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Open-Form Geometric Style Transfer
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A geometric style learned from one family of shapes is typically applied to new shapes from the same family. We consider a more challenging setting: learning the geometric design language of a stylized Latin alphabet and applying it to new forms, from Greek glyphs to entirely different structures such as human poses. We introduce Open-Form Geometric Style Transfer, where the forms to which a learned geometric style can be applied are not restricted to the shape family in which that style was observed. This setting is deceptively challenging: the difficulty is not merely learning a style, but learning the style without learning the shape family in which it was observed. We represent target forms by structural sketches and disentangle structural adherence from style realization using a Geometry LoRA and a style-specific LoRA. Critically, open-form transfer requires the Geometry LoRA to be universal. To achieve this, we devise a geometry-enrichment strategy that constructs a large and purposefully diverse collection of synthetic structural sketches spanning a broad range of unfamiliar geometries. Our experiments and ablations demonstrate the importance of both disentanglement and this universal geometry prior, enabling geometric styles learned from glyphs, pictograms, and other shape families to be transferred to substantially different, unseen forms.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Real-Time Radar Semantic and Panoptic Scene Understanding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Robust scene understanding under varying environmental conditions is essential for safe autonomous driving. While cameras and LiDAR degrade in adverse weather and poor lighting, Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) spinning radar provides dependable 360° perception at extended ranges with minimal compute cost. However, real-time FMCW radar scene understanding is challenging due to complex signal returns, limited temporal resolution, and scarce annotated datasets. We introduce StreamRPS, a novel framework for streaming FMCW radar panoptic segmentation, comprising an automated label-generation pipeline via LiDAR scene completion and a real-time streaming network for semantic and panoptic segmentation. Our encoder-decoder streaming architecture comprises a radar-specific hierarchical Transformer encoder and task-specific decoders for semantic or panoptic prediction. Our encoder introduces a stem to capture range-dependent signatures, anisotropic patch embeddings to preserve angular resolution, and axial polar attention to separately model the periodic azimuth and bounded range axes. We further introduce azimuth roll rotation augmentation to simulate ego-vehicle rotation during training. Comprehensive experiments on the SAX and BOREAS datasets validate both our auto-labeling methodology and streaming segmentation network against established baselines. We outperform the strongest baseline by at least 1.4pp while processing sectors at over 400 FPS in a 4-sector streaming setting. We additionally provide manual annotations for 100 SAX radar scans, enabling independent evaluation of the entire framework.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PICA-WAM: Visual Perturbation Invariance via Cross-Appearance Self-Alignment in World Action Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future video and generate actions, yet remain sensitive to task-irrelevant visual perturbations, i.e., changes in visual appearance that should not affect robot behavior. We identify a gap in conventional WAM training: video prediction encourages representations to preserve appearance information, while action generation does not explicitly enforce invariance to task-irrelevant appearance. Data augmentation exposes WAMs to such perturbations but does not require perturbed and nominal observations to produce consistent action representations, and alignment with external pretrained features does not guarantee the desired invariance. To address this gap, we propose PICA-WAM, a self-supervised training framework that casts perturbation invariance as an auxiliary cross-appearance self-alignment task for WAMs. An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher processes the nominal observation to provide a deeper-layer target, while the online WAM processes a perturbed observation and aligns its shallower-layer action representation to this target through a lightweight projection head. Across four strong WAMs evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-Plus, EBench, and a real robot, PICA-WAM consistently improves robustness under visual perturbations, preserves nominal performance in simulation, and raises the real robot success rate. PICA-WAM further reduces the sensitivity of video features to task-irrelevant appearance and its propagation into actions, as shown by paired layer-wise diagnostics. Code: https://github.com/YudeZou/PICA-WAM-release

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Existing world models can generate action-conditioned video from a single image. Many focus on camera movement, allowing users to explore the generated scene. However, navigation alone does not ensure that an action follows persistent rules when its outcome depends on state that is invisible in the current frame. We present Stateful Harness, a framework that separates world evolution from video rendering to support stateful and rule-governed interaction. It maintains an evolving world state under specified rules, renders each resulting event with a frozen video model, and uses the generated clip to update the world state for the next turn. At each turn, the harness resolves the action selected by the user and compiles the resulting event into an instruction, while a preview clip from an editable 3D scene provides spatial and camera guidance. To evaluate rule compliance, we build WorldState-Bench, a benchmark of 50 counterfactual twin pairs that share an initial frame and action but differ in hidden state and required outcome. Under rule-only prompting, the best of the 11 evaluated video backends produces the required endings for both cases in 32% of pairs. For MiniMax-H3, specifying the required endings raises this rate from 32% to 64%, while the full harness reaches 92% with the same frozen model. These results support separating rule execution from video rendering for world interactions with hidden state.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: What Language Adds, and at What Cost: Four Controlled Probes of Pathology Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision--language models (VLMs) promise to make computational pathology queryable and able to draft reports, but how much language adds beyond the vision backbone is unclear, because almost every system is evaluated by its developers on test sets of their own choosing. We grade published evidence by how it was produced and test four claims with controlled probes that reuse released checkpoints and public data, varying one input at a time. Report text adds prognostic signal: adding a frozen embedding of the stage-redacted report to a slide embedding raises the pooled C-index by 0.019 for progression-free interval and by 0.016 for overall survival across 1{,}633 TCGA patients, and restoring the stage statement adds nothing. Prompts add no measurable accuracy at inference: with features and pooling fixed, zero-shot classification is statistically indistinguishable from a supervised linear probe for lung and renal cancer subtyping. Slide-level question answering is barely grounded: SlideChat answers 74.82\% of SlideBench-VQA(TCGA) items correctly with the slide and 74.41\% without it, whereas its language backbone alone reaches 43.52\%. Paraphrasing leaves accuracy unchanged but flips 8--23\% of answers. Self-reported gains from agentic navigation and few-shot language priors cannot yet be attributed to language. Language thus adds real but narrow value, and we propose minimum controls that would expose these failure modes in future evaluations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. Existing multi-shot video generation approaches achieve strong consistency but still fall short in controllability. In this paper, we propose Mise-en-Video (MeV), a highly controllable multi-shot video generation framework that allows video creators to conduct staging the multi-shot in the 3D space and then generate the corresponding multi-shot video. To achieve this, our framework combines a hierarchical attention mechanism for multi-level narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for precise, per-shot spatial control. To support training and evaluation, we develop standardized annotation pipelines and construct a 160K-video dataset with hierarchical multi-shot texts and oriented 3D bounding boxes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeV consistently outperforms strong baselines in video quality, inter-shot consistency, and subject-level controllability.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Deep Learning-based Semantic Segmentation of Dental Radiographs: Comparative Evaluation of PSPNet, DeepLabv3, UNet, and UNet++
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Accurate and efficient analysis of dental radiographs has become increasingly important for disease diagnosis and clinical decision making. In particular, dental radiographs segmentation plays a critical role as it is challenging due to several reasons, such as low contrast, noise in the images, variations in the image quality, etc. Previous studies have primarily addressed these challenges using convolutional neural networks (CNN)-based models. However, direct comparison of these segmentation models is still challenging due to the variations among the experimental settings. Therefore, we mainly compared four segmentation models, including Pyramid Scene Parsing Network (PSPNet), DeepLabV3, UNet, and UNet++, through a fair, controlled experimentation setting under varying conditions such as image sizes and batch sizes. For this, we used 1269 dental radiography images, and prior to training, we implemented a series of preprocessing techniques. To assess the models, we used several metrics, including Dice coefficient (DICE), Intersection over Union (IoU), accuracy, precision, training and validation losses. According to our results, UNet++ demonstrated the highest IoU score of 0.6719, and a DICE value of 0.7869, showing superior results in terms of segmentation, specifically when configured with an image size of 300x300 and a batch size of 16.
